reply.text: `==` tests whether two objects have equal values, by calling the operands' `__eq__` method. `is` tests whether two names refer to the exact same object in memory, meaning their `id()` values match. Two equal values can be distinct objects: `[1, 2] == [1, 2]` is `True`, but `[1, 2] is [1, 2]` is `False`, because each literal creates a new list. Use `==` for value comparison and reserve `is` for identity checks, most commonly `x is None`. Avoid `is` for numbers and strings, since CPython caches some small ints and interned strings, so `is` may appear to work by accident and then fail on other values.
